attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated as fact.

semantics.note: Fair summary of the cheaper and competitive parts. It leaves out 'exist, they work', but those are trivial. A firm present-tense observation.

contract.note: Reading 'magnitudes' as at least 10x is ordinary, even generous. The result depends on the comparison set: peer models favour him, while a literal 'all of their models' reading brings in GPT-4o mini, which defeats it. The contract names both readings.

evidence.note: Third-party developer report in the period. It found V3 near Sonnet on simple tasks at about 2% of the cost, but weaker on complex work, so it gives only partial support for 'competitive'.
DeepSeek's own price page for V3 and R1 in the period. These prices are the baseline for every ratio.
o1 list price in the period puts R1 about 27x cheaper than OpenAI's peer reasoning model.
GPT-4o mini cost about the same as V3 at the discount and less than V3 at full price, so DeepSeek was not magnitudes cheaper across OpenAI's range.
Gemini Flash prices from August 2024, before the period. They suggest Gemini was not much more expensive, but this is context only.

reviews.rationale: Holds: R1 was about 27x cheaper than o1, and a third-party report put V3 at about 2% of Sonnet's cost. Fails: GPT-4o mini was priced at or below V3, so 'magnitudes cheaper' does not hold across OpenAI's models, and the Gemini comparison is unsupported in the period. 'Independently verified competitive' rests on one developer report with mixed findings.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post.

semantics.note: The draft's 'did not make their models more efficient' is broader than he wrote. In context, 'it' means DeepSeek-style efficiency under hard constraints, and he concedes both firms had efficiency teams. The contract narrows the scope correctly.

contract.note: The contract treats 'it' as DeepSeek-style efficiency and admits that the motive cannot be seen in public records. That is fair, but it leaves nothing that could be tested.

evidence.note: OpenAI's cheap GPT-4o mini shows some efficiency work. It says nothing about DeepSeek-style efforts or about why the firms acted as they did.

reviews.rationale: The claim is about motive and a counterfactual: they skipped efficiency because no pressure forced it. No public record can test that, and 'it' has no defined standard, so the claim cannot be scored. The one evidence item is context only.
